Neutral Citation No. - 2023:Ahc:145506
Court No. - 70
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 29704 of 2023

Applicant :- Jeetu Rathaur
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Surendra Prasad Mishra
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Gyanendra Singh Kanaujiya
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Surendra Prasad Mishra, learned counsel for the applicant; Sri Gyanendra Singh Kanaujiya, learned counsel for the opposite informant and Sri Kunwar Tejendra Bahadur, learned AGA for the State-respondent.

2. The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
567 of 2022, under Sections 498A, 304B IPC & Section 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Rasoolpur,
District Firozabad, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against the applicant and his family members and according to the FIR, marriage of the applicant was performed with the deceased on 27.2.2020 and after marriage, applicant and his family members tortured her for additional demand of dowry of Rs. Five lacs and on 22.2.2022, they have committed her murder.

4. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that the entire allegations made against the applicant are totally false and baseless and applicant only being husband of the deceased has been made Jeetu Rathaur vs State Of U.P. on 21 July, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/39726131/
1 accused in the present matter.

sentences.text: 5. He further submitted that in the FIR alongwith the applicant there are as many as eleven accused persons which shows that entire family of the applicant has been roped in the present matter.
6. He next submitted that actually some dispute arose between husband and wife and only due to this reason, wife of the applicant committed suicide.
He further submitted that autopsy report of the deceased also suggests that she died due to hanging.

7. Per contra, learned AGA as well as learned counsel for the informant opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that wife of the applicant died under abnormal circumstances in her matrimonial home within two years of her marriage and there is also allegation of demand of dowry, therefore,
applicant does not deserve bail.
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

9. Applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died under abnormal circumstances within two and half years of her marriage, in her matrimonial home and there is also allegation of demand of dowry.
10.

However, from the autopsy report of the deceased it reflects that she died due to hanging and learned counsel for the applicant also urged that deceased committed suicide but he failed to bring any good reason even for the suicidal death of the wife of the applicant.
11. Law is settled that suicidal death also attracts the provision of Section 304 B IPC, therefore, in my view applicant who is husband of the deceased is not entitled to be enlarged on bail.
12. Accordingly, the instant bail application stands rejected.

13. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
